title: The ReadySet: A Battery Built for People Who Sold Phone Charges
conflicts: Price: $150 (NBC/TechNewsDaily 2011, GOOD 2012) versus $300 (MIT Technology Review 2012, for the US Kickstarter kit with a panel); the story uses about $150. Units sold by mid-2012 agree at about 2,000 across MIT Technology Review, GOOD and GSMA. The $50-a-month income figure is Lin's own claim and is attributed to him; 13,000 ReadyPay sales in 2014 are Fenix's self-reported figure and are labelled as such. GSMA says Fenix tried a bicycle charger before the ReadySet, while 2011 reports describe the ReadySet itself as bicycle-chargeable; the story uses the 2011 description.
notes: Founding date and the November 2009 MTN pilot of 20 prototypes come from a Fenix-supplied timeline in the GSMA 2015 case; the design details come from 2011 reporting. Co-founder Brian Warshawsky is named in the founder field. Lin's earlier employer (Potenco) is mentioned only as 'a pull-cord power generator'; a podcast blurb saying his previous startup failed could not be confirmed from a loadable source.
